Sweep a rule through a set of values

Source: R/sensitivity.R
sensitivity.Rd

Runs capacity with one rule set to each of values in turn and returns a tidy table of the results, so the effect of a height limit, a recession plane angle or a site area per dwelling can be read or plotted. Each run after the first is incremental: only sites whose rules change are rebuilt.

Usage

sensitivity(
  x,
  rule,
  values,
  by = NULL,
  measures = c("floor_area", "dwellings"),
  ...
)

Arguments

x

A scenario().

rule

Path of the rule to change, as for set_rule(), such as "zones.MDR.ratios.coverage_max.value". A height is several linked values (total, occupiable, storeys); sweep it by giving whole height_limit()s as values, at path "zones.MDR.height".

values

The values to try: numbers, formulas as strings, or a list of whole rules (then value in the result is the position in the list).

by

Optional grouping, as for summarise_capacity().

measures

Measures, as for summarise_capacity().

...

Passed to estimate_capacity().

Value

A data frame of class plancap_sensitivity: value, the grouping columns, the measures, and floor_area_change and dwellings_change against the first value where those measures are asked for.

Examples

town <- exampleton()
sc <- scenario("Operative", rulebook_example("exampleton"),
               parcels = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "land", ],
               roads = town$parcels[town$parcels$parcel_type == "road", ],
               zoning = town$zoning, layers = town[c("height_areas", "transit")])
sensitivity(sc, "zones.MDR.ratios.coverage_max.value", c(0.4, 0.5, 0.6), by = "zone")
